questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Raise the bar
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Raise the bar
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'To set higher goals.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Raise the bar means to set higher rules or goals. (उच्च लक्ष्य निर्धारित करना)
    • Example: Celebrate what you've accomplished, but raise the bar a little higher each time you succeed.
  • From the given options, the second option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Raise the bar" that it is all about to lift or move a long rigid piece of wood, metal, or similar material.
     

Additional Information

  • This phrase originates in athletic terminology around the turn of the century. It is from the area of pole vault and high jump, where it is necessary to raise the bar after each jump to reach a new height record and increase the competition.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. To take a chill pill
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

To take a chill pill

options.text: To gulp a tablet for a cold
options.html: To gulp a tablet for a cold

options.text: To ask a doctor for medication
options.html: To ask a doctor for medication

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'To calm down'.

Key Points

  • An idiom is a group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words.
  • The phrase 'chill pill' (noun) refers to something that has a calming or relaxing effect. (कुछ ऐसा जिसका शांत या आराम देने वाला प्रभाव हो)
  • Therefore the idiom 'To take a chill pill' (often used imperatively) means to calm down; relax. (शांत होना; आराम करना)
    • Example: Stop shouting! Take a chill pill!
  • Hence option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. To walk on air
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

To walk on air
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'to be very happy'.

Key Points

  • An idiom is a group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words (e.g. over the moon, see the light ).
  • The idiom 'walk on air' means to feel extremely excited or happy.
    • Example: After the delivery of her baby, she was walking on air.
  • Therefore the idiom 'To walk on air' means 'to be very happy'.
  • Hence option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be at a loss for words
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Be at a loss for words
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Not know what to say.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Be at a loss for words means being uncertain of what to say, especially because you are very surprised or shocked. (क्या कहना है, इस बारे में अनिश्चित होना, खासकर इसलिए कि आप बहुत हैरान या चौंक गए हैं)
    • Example: She hesitated and briefly appeared at a loss for words.
  • From the given options, the first option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Be at a loss for words" that it is all about the one who lost the ability to speak or lost sound.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Want to curl up and die
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Want to curl up and die
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Feel terribly ashamed and sorry.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Want to curl up and die means to feel very ashamed and sorry. (बहुत शर्म और खेद महसूस करना)
    • Example: I just wanted to curl up and die when I spilled coffee on her new dress!
  • From the given options, the third option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Want to curl up and die" that it is all about someone wanting to stop living.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To cut a long story short
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To cut a long story short

options.text: Tell something in a roundabout way
options.html: Tell something in a roundabout way

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Tell something briefly'.

Key Points

  • The idiom 'to cut a long story short' means skipping extraneous or unnecessary details and getting to the point. (संक्षेप में कुछ बताना)
    • Example: My friend introduced me to her at a work function a year ago, and, to cut a long story short, we're moving in together next month.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom is 'tell something briefly'.
  • Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

Additional InformationLet's learn about other given options:

  • 'Be headed for' means to be in the process of doing something or travelling to some endpoint or destination. (कुछ करने या किसी अंतिम बिंदु या गंतव्य की यात्रा करने की प्रक्रिया में होना।)
    • Example: With the way, he keeps skipping school, Brian is definitely headed for trouble.
  • 'Straight from the shoulder' means very direct, without attenuation or embellishment. (बहुत प्रत्यक्ष, क्षीणन या अलंकरण के बिना)
    • Example: Sometimes he spoke straight from the shoulder and sometimes in puzzles.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Full of beans
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Full of beans

options.text: A dish made of French beans
options.html: A dish made of French beans

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'full of energy'.

Key Points

  • The idiom 'Full of beans' means to have a lot of energy and enthusiasm. (बहुत सारी ऊर्जा और उत्साह)
    • Example: She was laughing and shouting and generally full of beans.
  • Therefore the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom is 'full of energy'.
  • Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

Additional InformationLet's learn about some more idioms:

  • 'Full of prunes' means full of nonsense. (निरर्थक)
    • Example: You’re just silly, completely full of prunes.
  • 'Full of years' means old. (बूढ़ा)
    • Example: Because he is full of years, he's having a hard time getting around now.
  • 'Full to the gills' means completely full. (पूरी तरह से भरा)
    • Example: I've got so many meetings and deadlines these days that my schedule is full to the gills!

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. Apple of one's eye
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

Apple of one's eye
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Someone very precious or dear.
Key Points
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given idiom:-
  • Apple of one's eye -something or someone very precious or dear.
    • For Example - His new baby girl was the apple of his eye.
  • The apple of one’s eye describes a thing or person which someone loves above all others, someone’s favorite person or thing, a person or thing that he is proud of.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

Hinglish

  • आइए दिए गए मुहावरे का अर्थ देखें:-
  • Apple of one's eye - कोई वस्तु या कोई बहुत कीमती या प्रिय।
    • उदाहरण के लिए - His new baby girl was the apple of his eye.
  • किसी की आँख का तारा उस चीज़ या व्यक्ति का वर्णन करता है जिसे कोई अन्य सभी से ऊपर प्यार करता है, किसी का पसंदीदा व्यक्ति या चीज़, वह व्यक्ति या चीज़ जिस पर उसे गर्व है।
  • अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At the eleventh hour
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

At the eleventh hour
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'At the very last minute'.

Key Points

  • At the eleventh hour means At the very last minute; the latest possible moment.
  • Examples- 
    • Just minutes before the deadline, he definitely submitted his assignment at the eleventh hour.
    • It's very irresponsible to leave chores until the eleventh hour before doing them.
    • Lisa loves the thrill and rush of delivering parcels at the eleventh hour.
    • The lady was scolded for reporting for duty at the eleventh hour.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

The correct answer is 'A dream or idea that is unlikely to happen'.

  • Pipe dream: an unattainable or fanciful hope or scheme. (एक अप्राप्य या काल्पनिक आशा या योजना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Herculean task
questions.questionHtml:

Herculean task

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Spick and span
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Spick and span
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Neat and clean.

  • Spick and span means neat, clean, and well looked after.​ (साफ़ सुथरा)

options.html: Good massage for aches and pains

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. Wild goose chase
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

Wild goose chase

options.text: A safari to spot rare animals
options.html: A safari to spot rare animals

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'A worthless hunt or chase' 
Key Points 

  • The meaning of the given idiom is:
  • Wild goose chase means a complicated or lengthy and usually fruitless pursuit or search (एक जटिल या लंबी और आमतौर पर फलहीन खोज)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A stumbling block
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A stumbling block
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e., 'An obstacle to progress'.

Key Points

  •  A stumbling block is an idiom that means a circumstance that causes difficulty or hesitation.
    • ​Example - The country's water shortage was a stumbling block to investors.
  • So, an obstacle to progress is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 

Additional Information

  •  One word substitutions for the idiom a stumbling block include hurdle, barrier, impediment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A kick in the teeth
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A kick in the teeth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e., 'a grave setback'.

Key Points

  •   A kick in the teeth is an idiom that means something that is very shocking and disappointing. (कुछ ऐसा जो बहुत ही चौंकाने वाला और निराशाजनक है)
    • ​Example - Losing that game was a real kick in the teeth.
  • So, a grave setback is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 

Additional Information 

  •  One word substitutions for the idiom a kick in the teeth includes setback, letdown, shock.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. A live wire
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

A live wire

options.text: A very active or energetic person

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e., 'A very active or energetic person'.

Key Points

  •    A live wire is an idiom that means an energetic and unpredictable person. (एक ऊर्जावान और अप्रत्याशित व्यक्ति)
    • ​Example - She is a wonderful girl, a real live wire and full of fun.
  • So, a very active or energetic person is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 

Additional Information 

  •  One word substitutions for the idiom a live wire include fireball, bootstrapper, go-getter, highflier.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Fair and square
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Fair and square
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'According to the rules.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Fair and square mean according to the rules. (नियमों के अनुसार)
    • Example: The supporters of the other team were angry but we won the game fair and square.
  • From the given options, the second option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
 

Additional Information

  • The phrase fair and square dates back to the 1600s. It is usually used in the context of sporting competitions, races or, any kind of contest. It would be used especially to combat claims of cheating or dispute. It suggests that the proceedings were honest and all rules were adhered to.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Sit on the fence
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Sit on the fence
questions.solution: Sit on the fence means to delay or avoid making a decision or choice. For example: You can’t sit on the fence any longer, you need to make up your mind.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A bad egg
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A bad egg

options.text: Someone who is dishonest and unreliable
options.html: Someone who is dishonest and unreliable

options.text: Someone who likes to break eggs
options.html: Someone who likes to break eggs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Someone who is dishonest and unreliable.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: A bad egg means someone who is dishonest and unreliable. (बेईमान और अविश्वसनीय)
    • Example: At first I trusted him, but soon I found he's a bad egg.
  • From the given options, the first option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "A bad egg" that it is all about something related to a rotten egg.
     

Additional Information

  • The phrase was originated right in the mid-19th century. And the terms bad egg first appeared in print in the novel “Captain Priest” by Samuel A Hammett published in 1855.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On cloud nine

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A square deal

A square deal
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'A fair agreement.'

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To fight tooth and nail
